context: Read has_trailing_delimiter and patch the narrowest open/read operation used by that function so this single test raises PermissionError/OSError independent of effective uid and ACL model. Assert the exception propagates. Do not change product exception handling unless the reduced test proves a product defect.
description: tests/unit/utils/test_file_format.py::TestHasTrailingDelimiterSurfacesReadFailures::test_unreadable_file_raises_rather_than_reporting_clean fails on Windows because chmod(0o000) does not make a file unreadable under Windows ACL semantics. The product contract is still correct: has_trailing_delimiter must propagate an OSError from the read boundary rather than return False. Make the regression deterministic on every platform by injecting the read failure at the narrow file-open/read seam, while retaining missing-file and directory cases as real filesystem coverage.

anti_patterns.dont: Change product code to manufacture a permission check
anti_patterns.instead: Let the actual open/read error remain authoritative.
anti_patterns.why: Pre-checking mode bits is racy and does not model Windows ACLs.

anti_patterns.dont: Skip the test on Windows or when running as root
anti_patterns.instead: Inject PermissionError at the product's read boundary.
anti_patterns.why: The exception propagation contract is platform independent and can be tested deterministically.

preserves.behavior: A missing input path and a directory passed as a file still raise OSError through real filesystem operations.
Empty and blank-only readable files still return False.
The test remains green under root, ordinary POSIX users, and Windows.

verifications.description: Product file-format module is outside the patch

work_units.summary: Identify the exact open/read seam used by has_trailing_delimiter
Replace chmod-based unreadability with deterministic injected OSError
Run the file-format suite and confirm production code is untouched
